results.limitations: Diagnostic profile with a warmup in a disposable store/source copy. Single profiled run; not a repeated A/B performance claim. Parent retains setup state, so RSS is diagnostic only.

result_data.limitations: One real Babel corpus, dominated by parser/transformation fixtures. Does not establish general language completeness, large multi-repository throughput, warm-server latency or production SLOs. Cold builds, unchanged checks, deletion and fresh rebuild are correctness probes, not repeated performance estimates.
result_data.method: Fresh CLI/measurement processes, same admitted seed and absolute cache path; independent caches parked by rename. Five or more paired measured edits for the full corpus, one excluded warmup per arm, alternating arm order, warm OS cache. Setup and verification excluded from timings.

harness_selfcheck.note: E12 against itself on the 123-file smoke corpus while a release build ran. Correctness check only; timings excluded from performance conclusions.

invariants: Same worker count and existing minimum parallel batch size.
Change only start order, by descending file size; retain source positions for records, reports and deferred cache updates.
Metadata read failure never drops a file.
limitations: No competing builds, tests, fixture preparation or benchmarks were deliberately run during measured calls. Unrelated host load could not be verified; substantial timing drift occurred.
One real Babel corpus; no universal speed or language-completeness claim.
Candidate runtime and its added test were removed; the reusable comparison harness and evidence remain.
rationale: Reject the scheduling change. Only three of five measured edit pairs improve end-to-end time, with a median paired improvement of 1.38%; two regress. Extraction improves in three pairs and regresses in two. Whole-operation medians are distorted by substantial drift in phases unrelated to scheduling. Peak measured RSS is 1.56% higher. This does not demonstrate a useful, repeatable benefit for the target workload; it does not prove the heuristic is universally harmful.
